page: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-288-lssd is an x86_64 general-purpose instance powered by an Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor clocked at 2.3 GHz. The configuration delivers 288 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 144 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU package features a 504 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and advanced instruction sets including Intel AMX (amx_tile and amx_int8) alongside AVX-512 extensions. Memory is provisioned at 1080 GB RAM, reflecting approximately 3.75 GB of RAM per vCPU. Attached local storage consists of 19,296 GB of direct NVMe SSD capacity spread across 48 local SSD drives, with no dedicated GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses included.

Benchmark outcomes show top-tier multi-threaded compute, memory bandwidth, and I/O handling. In stress-ng, multi-core CPU performance reaches 312,171.7, placing it in the top 10% bracket, contrasted with average single-core throughput at 2,297.69. Large-block memory reads yield over 1,062 GB/sec, while cached small-block operations exceed 22,949 GB/sec. The instance delivers 407.31 million operations per second in Redis SET workloads and achieves 241.6 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. Instruction-heavy tasks such as PassMark extended instructions (376,095.0) and encryption benchmarks (320,564.3) register in the top 10%, aided by native hardware acceleration.

Hardware tradeoffs focus on raw parallelism over sequential latency. Single-threaded metrics, including baseline stress-ng execution and small-model LLM generation throughput, reflect the lower 2.3 GHz base frequency. However, prompt processing for 7B models achieves 307.21 tokens per second due to the large core pool and AMX matrix instructions. The integration of 19,296 GB NVMe SSD space pairs directly with the high CPU density, delivering cost efficiency by eliminating external network storage latencies for massive data tiers without requiring specialized accelerator silicon.

This instance profile is best suited for large-scale relational or NoSQL database clusters, in-memory caching systems such as Redis, large Clang compilation matrices, data transformation pipelines, and high-concurrency static web delivery where low-latency access to local NVMe storage and vast core counts are critical.

The system features a massive 504 MB L3 cache and supports Intel AMX and AVX-512 instruction sets. Benchmark testing demonstrates exceptional top-tier capabilities in multi-threaded execution, with multi-core stress-ng achieving 312,171.7, large-block memory read bandwidth exceeding 1,062 GB/sec, and Redis operations surpassing 407 million operations per second. While single-thread clock speed is modest, the dense compute footprint and high-throughput local NVMe storage deliver strong resource consolidation for demanding database architectures, high-volume caching, parallel compilation, and large-scale data transformation workloads.
